question:
For every positive integer \(n,\) let \(\operatorname{mod}_5(n)\) be the remainder obtained when \(n\) is divided by \(5.\) Define a function \(f : \{0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots\}\) \(\times \{0, 1, 2, 3, 4\}\) \(\to \{0, 1, 2, 3, 4\}\) recursively as follows:

\[ \tiny f(i, j) = \begin{cases} \operatorname{mod}_5(j + 1) & \text{if } i = 0 \text{ and } 0 \le j \le 4, \\ f(i - 1, 1) & \text{if } i \ge 1 \text{ and } j = 0, \text{ and} \\ f(i - 1, f(i, j - 1)) & \text{if } i \ge 1 \text{ and } 1 \le j \le 4. \end{cases} \]

What is \(f(2015, 2)?\)
solution:
For each fixed \(i\), there are only five values to track. Write them in order as
\[
R_i=(f(i,0),f(i,1),f(i,2),f(i,3),f(i,4)).
\]
Once the preceding row is known, the recursion determines the next row from left to right. Its first entry is the preceding row's entry with index \(1\). Each subsequent entry is found by using the value just obtained as an index into the preceding row. All these indices belong to \(\{0,1,2,3,4\}\), as required.

For example, when \(R_1=(2,3,4,0,1)\), the next row starts with
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(2,0)&=f(1,1)=3,\\
f(2,1)&=f(1,3)=0,\\
f(2,2)&=f(1,0)=2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Continuing the same lookup rule gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
R_0&=(1,2,3,4,0),\\
R_1&=(2,3,4,0,1),\\
R_2&=(3,0,2,4,1),\\
R_3&=(0,3,4,1,0),\\
R_4&=(3,1,3,1,3),\\
R_5&=(1,1,1,1,1).
\end{aligned}
\]
If a row consists entirely of \(1\)'s, the next row starts with \(1\), and every later lookup also returns \(1\). Thus an all-1 row always produces another all-1 row. Starting with \(R_5\), this proves that every row with index at least \(5\) is all \(1\)'s. Therefore \(f(2015,2)=\boxed{1}\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
